pr.title: Fetch each live checkout's default branch into Projector's own ref, so a merged policy applies within a full pass
pr.head: e47aa9e7b9394a1fc135d17927ca17625ca532d4

summary: Projector reads repository policy from the default branch. Until this change, that policy could remain stale until you fetched. The watch daemon now fetches each live registered checkout’s default branch on its worker pool, using a private Git ref instead of changing the remote-tracking refs you use.

Configuration reads the newer of the daemon’s fetched commit and your cached default branch. Your commit wins when the histories diverge. Fetch failures retain the previous commit and appear in watch status; watch.fetch_default = false disables the background fetch.

Git commands now discard inherited variables that could point them at another repository. The original two-checkout reproduction passes: a fetch requested for checkout B updates B’s private ref, leaves A untouched, and preserves B’s remote-tracking ref.

groups.title: Choose the refreshed policy commit
groups.kicker: Keep policy current without using the checked-out branch.
intro: The configuration reader finds both your origin/HEAD commit and the daemon’s refs/projector/default/ commit. A merge-base comparison chooses the fetched commit when it descends from yours, and chooses yours for divergent histories.
The comparison result is cached by the commit pair, alongside the existing configuration blobs. Repeated reads of an unchanged pair therefore avoid another Git process.

files.note: Adds the opt-out setting, resolves the private ref, and caches ancestry comparisons.

groups.title: Fetch on the daemon worker pool
groups.kicker: Schedule one repository fetch and report its result.
intro: On each full pass, the daemon gathers the repositories of live registered sessions and deduplicates linked worktrees by their common Git directory. It skips repositories that opt out and submits the rest to the relay’s worker pool, so the network operation does not run on the event loop.

The fetch uses an empty --refmap=, disables tags and submodules, and writes only Projector’s private destination ref. Completion updates the per-checkout status; a failure preserves the previous policy commit. An outstanding fetch also keeps the daemon from exiting for idleness.

The shared Git runner removes inherited Git-location variables before running a command. This keeps both the default-branch fetch and the relay’s existing reads and writes in the checkout named by the caller; its explicit commit-identity environment still applies.

checks.text: The original two-checkout reproduction passes with GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE naming checkout A while fetching B. B receives the new private ref, A receives none, and B’s origin/main stays unchanged. Existing relay tests also pass.

files.note: Runs each Git command in its named checkout by removing inherited variables that redirect repository, worktree, index, object storage, or namespace.
Schedules and collects background fetches, exposes status, and waits for running fetches before idle exit.
Prints each checkout’s default-branch fetch state and error in watch status.
Adds full-pass regressions for policy freshness, preserved user refs, force-push preference, failed fetches, opting out, and an inherited Git environment.

checks.text: The 152 focused watch/configuration/relay tests passed. The new two-checkout full-pass regression verifies the requested checkout receives the fetched ref and the other repository receives none.
